findings.title: Compiler SIGSEGV: funcInstance returns NULL after the type-depth diagnostic, callers dereference it (deep explicit type argument)
findings.why: funcInstance promises 'NULL when tmpl is NULL' in its doc comment, but it also returns NULL on the two error paths (type depth > TYPE_DEPTH_LIMIT at line 4534, and c->funcInsts.len >= FUNC_INST_LIMIT at line 4544) after only reporting a diagnostic. Its callers do not check: check_expr.c:2404-2405 does 'FuncDef *inst = funcInstance(...); inst->used = true;' and check_expr.c:3179-3180 does the same. The invariant 'the return value is dereferenceable' is not established by the diagnostic path, so the compiler segfaults while trying to report the limit -- the exact input class the limit was added for (tools/attack.py E3, comment at check_top.c:4480-4494). Only resolveDeferredCall (check_top.c:5013-5014) checks for NULL.
findings.trigger: Any explicit type argument whose instantiation nesting is deeper than TYPE_DEPTH_LIMIT (64), e.g. z<box<box<...65+...<i64>...>>>(). Also any program that creates 4096 distinct generic instances at an EX_GENCALL/EX_CALL site (the same unchecked call path). Both unchecked call sites are live: check_expr.c:2405 (EX_GENCALL, depth limit) and check_expr.c:3180 (ordinary call after the GENCALL rewrite, instance-count limit).

findings.title: UNSOUND: the deferred zero-value check is never recorded for free generic functions -> silently zero-initializes a `fn` field (null code pointer) or emits an undeclared marker
findings.why: This branch is the only place a deferred zero-value check is decided, and the only way to reach it for a free-function instance is check_top.c:5775-5782 with refCheckApplies() (check_top.c:4819-4823), which requires rc->func == fi->tmpl, i.e. an instance of a free generic function. But every recorder refuses free functions: recordZeroCheck (check_escape.c:1496-1497), recordNewSizeCheck (1474-1475) and recordRefCheck (1527-1530) all start with 'if (!c->curFunc || !c->curFunc->owner) return;', and owner is NULL for a free function (only parser.c:895 and check_top.c:5472 set it). So no record can ever exist for a free template and the free-instance replay path is dead; the check the concrete path performs (check_stmt.c:253-266 'cannot zero-initialize ...') is simply skipped after instantiation. codegen then falls into zeroValue's defensive lines (codegen.c:1608-1623): the `ref` marker makes gcc fail, but a struct containing a `fn` field takes the '(name){0}' fast path and silently produces a null function pointer.
findings.trigger: A free generic function with an uninitialized local of type T, instantiated with a type that has no zero value: (a) T = a struct containing `fn(i32)->i32` -> accepted and emits `(cellfn){0}` (null code pointer, calling it jumps to address 0); (b) T = slice<u8> or a struct containing a `ref` -> emitted C names __extc_reference_has_no_zero_value__ and does not compile. The same program written concretely is rejected with the correct diagnostic.
findings.repro: (a) /tmp/f3.extc: 'struct cellfn { f: fn(i32) -> i32 }\nfn mk<T>() -> T { var b: T  return b }\nfn main() -> i32 { let c: cellfn = mk<cellfn>()  return c.f(3) }'; ./build/extc /tmp/f3.extc -o /tmp/f3.c && gcc -O0 -o /tmp/f3 /tmp/f3.c && /tmp/f3 -> Segmentation fault, rc=139 (the emitted body is 'cellfn b = (cellfn){0};'). (b) /tmp/t1.extc ('fn mk<T>() -> T { var b: T  return b }' instantiated with slice<u8>) -> ./build/extc /tmp/t1.extc --check-c -> "error: '__extc_reference_has_no_zero_value__' undeclared". Controls rejected correctly: /tmp/f1c.extc (concrete cellfn) -> "cannot zero-initialize `b`: it contains a `fn`"; /tmp/t0.extc (concrete slice<u8>) -> "it contains a reference"; the method version (/tmp/f2.extc) is rejected per instance by runRefCheck.

findings.title: MISCOMPILE: deferred generic call sites are resolved in a single pass, so a 3-deep generic chain calls the never-emitted provisional instance f_T (declaration-order dependent)
findings.why: Each CallCheck is visited exactly once (c.callChecks is never iterated again), and resolveDeferredCall can only instantiate when an instance of the *enclosing* template already exists (line 5602). Records are appended in body-check order, so when the inner template is declared before the outer one, the record for the innermost call is processed before the record that creates the enclosing instance: g_i64 is created only later, and the already-visited innermost record is never revisited, leaving node->func pointing at the provisional f_T (which codegen deliberately never emits). The comment at 5574-5581 claims this batch must run before the requirement batches, but there is no fixed point inside it; running to a fixed point (or resolving in dependency order) is what the shape requires.
findings.trigger: A generic function whose body calls another generic function, called from a third generic function, where the inner template is declared before the outer one: main -> m<i64> -> g<i64> -> f(...) with the source order f, g, m. Reversing the declaration order makes it work, which proves the pass is order-dependent.

findings.title: MISCOMPILE: a coroutine whose body has no `yield` skips coroFrameLay's field layout, so the generated frame struct has no members
findings.why: coroSetup (check_top.c:3959-4012) has already created the frame struct and made it the function's return type; coroFrameLay is the only place that fills that struct with pc/ret/zone/task/in/arenaN and the captured parameters (lines 6807-6868). Returning at line 6750 for a body with no yield leaves fsd->fields empty while codegen still emits the protocol bodies and the frame accesses (f->pc, f->arena1, f->n, ...), because 'isCoro' is true independently of whether a yield was written. The early return's justification ('nothing to lay out') is false: the frame shape is needed whether or not the coroutine ever suspends.
findings.trigger: A coroutine function with no `yield` statement in its body, spawned from anywhere, e.g. 'fn c(n: i64) -> coroutine<i64> { var i: i64 = 0 }' plus 'var h = c(i64(3))  var b: bool = h.next()'.
findings.repro: /tmp/c1.extc: 'fn c(n: i64) -> coroutine<i64> { var i: i64 = 0 }\nfn main() -> i32 { var h = c(i64(3))  var b: bool = h.next()  return 0 }'; ./build/extc /tmp/c1.extc --check-c -> "error: 'struct c$frame' has no member named 'pc'", "no member named 'arena1'", "no member named 'n'" + "the generated C does not compile".

findings.title: HYGIENE: allFunctions lists every `impl` method twice (already attached to StructDef.methods), so all four all-passes do the work twice and the 'one owner' list has already drifted
findings.why: The impl attachment already pushes each method into its target's method set (checkModule, check_top.c:5472-5473 'mth->owner = sd; vecPush(&sd->methods) = mth;') without removing it from im->methods, so the third loop adds those same FuncDef pointers a second time. Every consumer of `all` then processes them twice: the needsHome recompute, the four computeEscapes rounds, the union pass, the site-placement loop, the refDepth sync and the owSites/owLocal loop. The pass is idempotent today, but the comment above ('Spelling it out in one place is the point ... which is how one copy quietly falls out of step with the others') is already false: the @inline check at 5868-5875 builds a third list (m->funcs + structs, no impls) by hand.
findings.trigger: Any program with an `impl` block: each of its methods appears twice in the same `all` vector.
findings.repro: struct counter { i: i64  n: i64 } + 'impl counter { fn zzNext(self: mut ref counter) -> bool { ... } }' (/tmp/impl2.extc): EXTC_DBG_HOME=1 ./build/extc /tmp/impl2.extc -o /dev/null | grep -c "\[home\] zzNext" -> 2, and the two lines are adjacent (dump lines 50 and 51), i.e. one `all` vector holding the same method twice.

findings.title: HYGIENE: two copies of the coroutine handle-protocol synthesis disagree on the receiver mutability of `send` (and on modName)
findings.why: The same three handle methods are synthesized in two places from the same hw[3]={3,4,6} table: coroSetup (check_top.c:3901-3954) and the checkModule pre-pass (check_top.c:5167-5219). For `send` (which==6) coroSetup produces a read-only receiver (mut=false) while the pre-pass produces a mutable one (mut=true), and only the pre-pass sets pm->modName (the coroSetup copy also leaves it NULL). Method-call legality (a mut method may not be called through a `let` binding) therefore depends on which copy ran. In today's pipeline the prelude is checked first (main.c loadPrelude -> checkModule), so hsd->methods.len != 0 by the time coroSetup runs and the coroSetup copy is dead -- the divergence is silent and will become a behavior change if the synthesis order ever changes.
findings.trigger: Any coroutine handle use of `send` (the pre-pass copy wins today); the divergence becomes observable if the on-demand synthesis in coroSetup is ever the one that runs (e.g. a module checked before the prelude, or a handle struct whose methods are not synthesized by the pre-pass).
findings.repro: Static: compare check_top.c:3942 with check_top.c:5207 (and check_top.c:3931 vs 5195-5199 for modName). I could not construct an input where the coroSetup copy runs (the prelude is always checked first), so this is a latent divergence, not an observed miscompile.

coverage_notes: Read all of src/check_top.c:3441-5160 line by line (and continued to 6885 for the whole checkModule). In-range functions audited: levelPass (fixed-point/alias walk; monotone lowering and the 64-round cap look right, no repro of a wrong placement), the checkOpenHandles family (typeIsResource/obligFind/obligEscapeAll/obligExpr/obligStmt/checkOpenHandles: flow-insensitive, escape-by-default on unknown shapes, aliases handled; tried resource locals, aliases, returns, fields, nested blocks - no wrong diagnostic found), the symbol index (sgHash/symBucket/symIdxSync: reset on arena/first-symbol/shrink and permanent fallback on a full 16-probe window; the two write-back paths in checkFunc are equivalent because cnameEq is just pointer-or-strcmp, and the fallback's dfLookup is NULL-safe), coroSetup, checkFunc (early returns for builtin/lambda/coroProto/extern checked against every body-less FuncDef producer), isConstInit (spot-checked against codegen's static-initializer needs), checkGlobals (duplicate names, zero-init with refs, non-constant initializers: /tmp/gl1..gl5 behave as documented, no crash on the curArenaSites path), funcInstance, unifyTParams (all TY_PARAM producers set `param`), runOpCheck/runDeferredUse/runMethodCheck (node kinds and non-NULL fields verified at their recording sites in check_expr.c/check.c), refCheckApplies/runRefCheck, provisionalInstance/resolveDeferredCall, roundMakesPool and the start of checkModule. Findings 3 and 4 are at check_top.c:5596 and 6750, just past my assigned range, but they are in the same file and I verified them with repros; findings 1, 2, 5, 6 are inside the range (1 is funcInstance, 2 is runRefCheck/refCheckApplies, 5 is allFunctions, 6 is coroSetup). Things checked and found correct: the deferred-call re-resolution for 2-level generics, the method-instance ref recheck (/tmp/f2.extc correctly rejected), the effect-summary union via mentionsParam (a free generic borrowed store IS caught at the call site: /tmp/t4.extc rejected), the globals checks, and symIdxSync's fallback equivalence. One thing I could not turn into a failure: internLocalTypes (check_top.c:4952-4973) omits ST_DOMAIN from its child walk while astWalkStmtChildren includes it, but a local `var p: pair<T>` inside a `d.run { }` block still emits pair_i64 correctly (/tmp/dom1.extc vs /tmp/dom0.extc), so I did not report it.
